prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a coarse kitchen layout: upper cabinets and the nearby counter/sink occupy the left and foreground, while the refrigerator and rear doorway lie farther ahead; the other person appears about 1–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer in frames 3–5, with the refrigerator roughly another 0.5–1 m behind him. Bright regions mark nearby surfaces, making the camera wearer’s foreground arms/hands and changing clearance to cabinets easier to distinguish than in RGB alone; these are generally within arm’s reach, about 0.2–0.7 m. Across the strip, the viewpoint turns from the sink/counter toward the person and refrigerator, while the person remains at a broadly similar distance and shifts from right-of-centre toward centre before returning rightward. Depth near silhouettes, dark recesses, frame edges, reflective appliances, and the person’s overlapping arms is unreliable, and several abrupt brightness changes appear to be estimation errors rather than real distance discontinuities.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates some foreground entities from the background, most consistently identifying the other person in frames 3–5 and the refrigerator behind and to his right at approximately 1.5–2.5 m from the camera wearer. It also isolates parts of the camera wearer’s arms/hands low in the frames, showing that they are much nearer than the standing person and sometimes overlap or occlude his lower body; the standing person’s hands are held in front of his torso and are within his own arm’s reach. The person is mostly front-facing or obliquely facing the camera wearer, with his head directed generally toward the camera in the later frames, while cabinetry lies above and the counter/sink remains lower and left as the camera pans right. The map is highly unreliable for object identity and completeness: cabinets or counters are labelled as “microwave,” “bed,” or “keyboard,” sinks are fragmented, several objects are missed, and masks are clipped by occlusion and the image boundaries.
descriptions.pose: The pose map makes articulated geometry clearest in frames 3–5: the standing person is roughly 1–1.5 m ahead, facing mostly toward the camera wearer, with head keypoints above a torso skeleton and bent arms/hands positioned in front of his chest. Magenta hand landmarks distinguish his hands from the camera wearer’s nearer hand entering from the left/lower foreground, clarifying that the two sets of hands are separated in depth and are not touching; each person’s visible hands remain within that person’s own arm span. Across these frames the person’s torso changes from a more angled profile to a more frontal orientation, while his image position shifts from right-of-centre to centre and back toward the right as the viewpoint turns. The map provides little scene layout or metric distance by itself, misses poses entirely in the first two frames, omits legs and many occluded joints, and contains unstable or floating head/hand points where limbs overlap or leave the view.
